name: Remo of the Blanco river
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

sources.citation: Fleck, David W. 2013. Panoan languages and linguistics. Anthropological Papers of the American Museum of Natural History 99. New York: AMNH.
sources.note: Nothing for this variety. Table 1: 'Remo of the Blanco River' = independent member of the Nawa Group; table 7: 179 items, Leuque (1927); appendix 2: 'Leuque (1927: 538-540) list of 179 words and phrases' is the entire documentation; appendix 1 synonymy (var. Rhemu; hom. Nukini); appendix 3 location. The remark 'all stress marks are left out, due to the inconsistency with which these are applied' (p. 4) concerns Fleck's spelling of language names, not Remo.

sources.citation: Fabre, Alain. 2005-. Diccionario etnolingüístico y guía bibliográfica de los pueblos indígenas sudamericanos: Pano-Takana (entry REMO/ISKONAWA)
sources.note: Nothing; lists 'Philips Leuque, F.E. 1927. Algunos términos y frases en el idioma remo' in the bibliography only.

sources.citation: Loukotka, Čestmír. 1968. Classification of South American Indian languages. Los Angeles: UCLA Latin American Center. p. 170
sources.note: Nothing; classification entry 'Nucuini or Remo or Rheno' citing Carvalho 1931 and 'Leuque in Izaquirre 1922-1929, vol. 13, pp. 538-540' (conflates the three Remo varieties).

sources.citation: Izaguirre, Bernardino (ed.). 1929. Historia de las misiones franciscanas.., vol. XIV. Lima. (archive.org historiadelasmis14izag)
sources.note: No Remo material; only the cumulative index line 'Algunos términos y frases en el idioma Remo 538'.

sources.citation: Philips Leuque, Enrique. 1927. Algunos términos y frases en el idioma remo. In Bernardino Izaguirre (ed.), Historia de las misiones franciscanas y narración de los progresos de la geografía en el oriente del Perú, vol. XIII: Producciones en lenguas indígenas de varios misioneros, 538-540. Lima: Talleres tipográficos de la Penitenciaría. (= Glottolog ref 147134, cited there from the 2002 2nd edn, vol. VI, 532-534)
sources.note: Nothing. A bare two-column list of 179 Spanish glosses with Remo forms in Spanish-based spelling; no prologue, no orthographic or pronunciation note. A few forms carry a written accent or diaeresis (Üpaha, Üjui, Sinú, anataí, Mahaí) as raw data only; no rule stated.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid record remo1250 (Hammarström et al.), with justification text and Glottolog's most extensive description entry
sources.note: No content; Glottolog's fullest description is only a wordlist (Leuque 2002 [1927], 3 pp.); 0 grammar/phonology/sketch references; the only other refs are Fleck 2013 and Oliveira 2023 (classification).
Nothing; says only that it was documented by Father Leuque, 'the first Remo language ever recorded'.

sources.citation: Oliveira, Sanderson Castro Soares de. 2023. Las primeras escisiones de la familia Pano: una propuesta de subagrupamiento en una familia de la Amazonia occidental. International Journal of American Linguistics 89(3): 289-331.
